title: These Extremists Are Running for Election in November
gist: A WIRED review finds hundreds of Republican midterm candidates with extremist ties, including 500+ state legislative candidates in far-right Facebook groups, amid rising political violence; it highlights races such as Texas Railroad Commissioner, where favorite Bo French would oversee Texas oil, gas and data center power decisions.

insights.claim: Over 500 candidates for state legislative seats in November are members of far-right Facebook groups promoting militias, gun rights and Christian nationalism, per data from the Institute for Research and Education on Human Rights.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
entities: Institute for Research and Education on Human Rights
insights.so_what: Rising extremist representation in state legislatures could shift state-level policy and political risk.
insights.locator: At a local level, over 500 candidates

insights.claim: Former GWU extremism researcher Luke Baumgartner argues extremist candidates are emulating the Trump administration, which he says has handed them a permission slip for formerly unthinkable rhetoric.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.so_what: Normalization at the top suggests extremist candidacies will persist beyond this cycle.
insights.quote: the executive branch has handed them a permission slip

insights.claim: While some extremist candidates such as James Fishback and Dan Bilzerian lost GOP primaries, many reached the general election and a number are expected to win.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.so_what: Election outcomes may add volatility to legislative agendas.

insights.claim: Terrorism and targeted violence incidents rose 19 percent in 2025 versus 2024 per University of Maryland researchers, and Capitol Police threat cases against members of Congress rose 58 percent, the third straight annual increase.

insights.so_what: Escalating political violence is a growing US social-stability and governance risk.

insights.claim: The US Marshals Service documented threats against almost 400 judges, roughly a 5 percent increase from the previous year.

themes.theme: Texas Railroad Commission and energy oversight

insights.claim: The Texas Railroad Commissioner oversees the state's oil and gas industry, which drills more hydrocarbons than the rest of the US combined, and will be critical to deciding how Texas's growing data center industry is powered.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.so_what: The seat directly affects US oil and gas regulation and data center power supply decisions.
insights.quote: The role will also be critical to deciding how the burgeoning data center industry in Texas will be powered.

insights.claim: GOP candidate Bo French, who has called for removing 100 million people from America and posted racist comments, is a slim favorite for Texas Railroad Commissioner per new polling, despite Karl Rove saying he would vote Democrat instead.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.so_what: An extremist regulator over Texas energy and data center power could add regulatory unpredictability.

insights.claim: Mark Lamb, tied to paramilitary groups and the constitutional sheriffs movement and backed by Trump and Turning Point USA, is almost certain to win Arizona's deeply red 5th District.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.so_what: Adds to the bloc of hard-right House members.

insights.claim: Trump-endorsed 'guntuber' Brandon Herrera, with a history of sexist and antisemitic remarks, is in a tight race for Texas's 23rd District against Democrat Katy Padilla Stout.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.so_what: Competitive seat relevant to House control.

insights.claim: In Georgia's Senate race, polling shows Democrat Jon Ossoff comfortably leading Trump-endorsed Mike Collins, whose campaign has been dogged by staff ties to white supremacists.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.so_what: Senate control math relevant to policy outlook.

insights.claim: Marshall Rawson, who marched at Charlottesville's Unite the Right rally, won a Florida House GOP primary in a district Republicans won by 48 points in 2024.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.so_what: Shows extremist candidates can win safe seats via low-visibility primaries.
